UV-induced replication fork arrest and restart is similar to that of hydroxyurea, with one important difference: UV-damaged replication forks restart effectively in a Polη-independent manner, while hydroxyurea-induced replication forks restart only in a Polη-dependent manner.

replication fork restart in human cells after UV irradiation does not require the translesion polymerase, Polη.
